newsitem.title: JAPAN: All Tokyo corn futures end limit-up on USDA data.
newsitem.headline: All Tokyo corn futures end limit-up on USDA data.

text.p: All Tokyo corn futures contracts ended up the daily 400 yen limit on Monday, after USDA crop reports pushed up the Chicago market on Friday, traders said.
The benchmark January 1998 contract ended up 400 yen at 14,800 yen per tonne, unchanged from the opening.
"Price rallies in Chicago triggered panic buying here from the opening. The sentiment remained bullish throughout the day," a brokerage house trader said.
The CBOT corn market soared on Friday, as the USDA pegged 1996 U.S. corn production at 9.293 billion bushels, which was below average trade expectations of 9.317 billion.
Corn stocks as of next September 1 were set at 959 million bushels from the previous 1.157 billion bushels.
The yen's weaker tone against the dollar also encouraged investors to buy, traders said.
As of 0805 GMT, the spot March corn contract on the CBOT Project A system was last traded at $2.65-1/2 per bushel, unchanged from Friday's Chicago close.
Spot January CBOT soybean futures on Project A were at $7.26-3/4, unchanged from Friday's close. Spot January CBOT wheat futures were at $3.87, unchanged from Friday.
